title: A finitely generated universal quotient flattening ideal over a henselian local base
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$, and suppose $A$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Assume $B$ is essentially of finite presentation over $A$, meaning that $B$ is a localization of a finitely presented commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and let $P$ be a finitely presented $B$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. There exists a finitely generated ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ such that, for every ideal $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, the $A/J$-module $P/JP$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] if and only if $I\subseteq J$. Here $JP$ is the submodule generated by products $ax$ with $a\in J$ and $x\in P$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Tag 05PG (theorem-flattening-local), specialization to local quotient maps A to A/J; finite generation is the final assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-henselian-pointed-devissage-chart] to obtain $C,N,D$ and the marked chain $(S_i,T_i,M_i,\alpha_i,\mathfrak p_i,\mathfrak q_i)$. The finite-presentation hypotheses imply finite type and finite generation by taking the images of the finite presentation generators. For each $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, base change makes $B/JB\to D/JD$ faithfully flat, so $P/JP$ is $A/J$-flat exactly when $N_{\mathfrak q}/JN_{\mathfrak q}$ is, by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change] and [lem-trf-flatness-faithfully-flat-extension]. Here $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto ax\bmod J$ identifies quotient and tensor modules, with inverse $x\bmod J\mapsto x\otimes1$; right exactness verifies that the kernel is $JP$. Finite unique-prime localization [lem-trf-unique-prime-localization] identifies $N_{\mathfrak q}$ with $(M_1)_{\mathfrak q_1}$: first use the surjection $C\to S_1$, then the finite map $T_1\to S_1$ and its unique prime above $\mathfrak q_1$. The same argument identifies $(\operatorname{coker}\alpha_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}$ with $(M_{i+1})_{\mathfrak q_{i+1}}$. These identifications commute with reducing modulo $J$, since fractions and the displayed tensor maps do.

source.place: Tag 05PG, first two proof paragraphs; algebra.tex Tags 0584 and 00EA.

proof.text: Work backwards along the fixed finite chain. We construct ideals $I_i\subseteq\mathfrak m$ such that for every $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, $(M_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}/J(M_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is flat over $A/J$ exactly when $I_i\subseteq J$, and such that the entire module $M_i/I_iM_i$ is projective over $A/I_i$. For the terminal cokernel $Q_n=0$ take the ideal $0$; the zero module is a summand of the free module of rank zero. For $i<n$ the induction hypothesis for $M_{i+1}$ supplies these two assertions for $Q_i=\operatorname{coker}\alpha_i$, using Step 1 for the localized assertion and the chain's global cokernel isomorphism for projectivity. If the chain has length zero, $N=0$ and the original module is zero by faithful flatness; take $I=0$ and stop.

source.place: Tag 05PG, induction on devissage length, with global projectivity retained as an induction invariant.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and write $K$ for the tail ideal of $Q_i$. If $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ makes the localized $M_i/JM_i$ flat over $A/J$, apply [lem-trf-local-generic-basis-universal-injective] to $A/J\to T_i/JT_i$ at $\mathfrak q_i/JT_i$. It makes $\alpha_i\bmod J$ universally injective and the localized $Q_i/JQ_i$ flat. Thus $K\subseteq J$ by induction. The hypotheses of that lemma hold after this quotient: flatness is preserved by base change; a finite algebra presentation reduces coefficientwise; the fibres are the same geometrically integral fibres as before. The residue fibre and the map at its generic point are unchanged since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The marked prime still lies over the closed point. These statements also follow by tensoring the complete devissage, as in [lem-sfb-complete-algebra-devissage-base-change]; its unpointed generic-basis data suffice here, and the quotient map carries the marked primes to their quotients.

source.place: Tag 05PG, subfunctor paragraph, using Tag 05I3 (1) implies (2) and Tag 05HJ for base change.

proof.text: Set $R=A/K$, and use bars for tensoring the stage with $R$. The module $\bar Q_i$ is projective over $R$ by induction. Let $E=\operatorname{im}(\bar\alpha_i)$. The exact sequence $0\to E\to\bar M_i\to\bar Q_i\to0$ splits over $R$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ses-projective-quotient-splits]. Put $F=\bar T_i^{\oplus r_i}$ and let $v:F\twoheadrightarrow E$ be the map induced by $\bar\alpha_i$. By [lem-trf-local-fibres-integral-projective], $\bar T_i$ is projective over $R$: the flat finite presentation and geometric integrality hypotheses were checked in Step 3. Taking $r_i$ copies of a split embedding into a free module gives $j:F\to G=\bigoplus_{t\in U}R$, $s:G\to F$ with $sj=1$. Let $L\subset R$ be generated by every coordinate of $j(x)$ for every $x\in\ker v$. This is a specified ideal, with no finiteness claim yet.

source.place: Tag 05PG, final existence paragraph; Tag 05PE coefficient construction replaces the appeal to 05PF.

proof.text: For any $R$-algebra $H$, right exactness applied to $\ker v\to F\to E\to0$ makes $v_H$ surjective with kernel the image of $(\ker v)\otimes_R H$. Since $j_H$ stays split injective, this kernel vanishes exactly when every coordinate of every $j(x)$ vanishes in $H$. Indeed $G\otimes_R H$ is free on the same basis, by the mutually inverse maps $e_t\otimes h\mapsto he_t$ and $e_t\mapsto e_t\otimes1$. Thus $v_H$ is an isomorphism exactly when $L$ maps to zero in $H$. The split sequence of Step 4 stays split after tensoring, so $\bar\alpha_i\otimes_R H$ is injective exactly when $v_H$ is an isomorphism. This proves the coefficient criterion directly, including rings with nilpotents; no assertion about the finite generation of $\ker v$ is used.

Let $I_i$ be the inverse image of $L$ in $A$. Apply Step 3 with $J=\mathfrak m$: every module over $A/\mathfrak m$ is flat, so $K\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and $\alpha_i\bmod\mathfrak m$ is injective. Step 5 then gives $I_i\subseteq\mathfrak m$. If a general $J$ makes the localized $M_i/JM_i$ flat, Step 3 gives $K\subseteq J$ and injectivity of $\alpha_i\bmod J$, so Step 5 gives $I_i\subseteq J$. Conversely, at $H=R/L=A/I_i$, Step 5 identifies $E\otimes_R H$ with $\bar T_i^{\oplus r_i}\otimes_R H$. Hence the split sequence gives $M_i/I_iM_i\cong(T_i/I_iT_i)^{\oplus r_i}\oplus(Q_i/I_iQ_i)$. Both summands are projective: the first by Step 4 and scalar extension, and the second by induction and scalar extension. Their direct sum is projective. For $J\supseteq I_i$ it stays projective over $A/J$, hence flat; localization at $\mathfrak q_i$ preserves base flatness. This proves both induction assertions.

source.place: Tag 05PG, end of existence argument; stronger projectivity invariant via split sums, as in Tag 05I4.

proof.text: Take $I=I_1$. Step 1 and the induction give the desired equivalence for all $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, initially without finite generation. In particular $P/IP$ is flat over $A/I$. Let $I_\lambda$ run through the finitely generated subideals of $I$. This is a nonempty directed set: $0$ is present and $I_\lambda+I_\mu$ contains both; its union is $I$ since each $a\in I$ lies in $(a)$. Apply [lem-sfb-fp-quotient-flatness-directed-limit] to obtain one $I_\lambda$ with $P/I_\lambda P$ flat. Our already proved equivalence forces $I\subseteq I_\lambda$, so $I=I_\lambda$ is finitely generated. This argument uses finite presentation over $B$, not finite presentation over $A$, and imposes no Noetherian assumption.

source.place: Tag 05PG, final proof paragraph, using Tag 05MN (2).

proof_origin.place: Tag 05PG (theorem-flattening-local), quotient-base specialization; existence by pointed devissage induction and the explicit coefficient construction of Tag 05PE in place of 05PF; stronger split-projectivity invariant follows the same induction as 05I4. Finite generation is exactly the final 05MN limit argument.

The item's statement is unchanged; it is 05PG specialised to A'=A/J, where the test set of primes is the single maximal ideal of B/JB. The delivery replaces the source's 05I4/05PF step (freeness of the cokernel, then the étale iso-locus theorem) with a stronger induction invariant: M_i/I_iM_i is projective over A/I_i. Over that split projective presentation the 05PE coefficient ideal applies directly. I checked Steps 3-6 and the argument is correct. Step 1: faithfully-flat base change (B/JB→D/JD) plus 0584 descent; 00EA unique-prime localisation and C→S_1 surjective give N_q≅(M_1)_{q_1}. Step 3: all hypotheses of the 05I3 node hold after reducing mod J (fibres over primes containing J, residue field of mT_i unchanged, M_i finite over T_i via S_i). Step 4: 05FT applies to A/K→T_i/K. Step 5: both directions of the coefficient criterion are right, and the step really is elementary. Step 6: J=m gives I_i⊆m; the converse uses the decomposition (T_i/I_i)^r⊕Q_i/I_i and scalar extension of projectives. Step 7 is exactly the last paragraph of 05PG. Edge cases: k[ε] with P=k gives I=(ε); r_i=0; length 0. New node henselian-pointed-devissage-chart is true: 05I1 plus the 04GG retraction with q'=τ⁻¹(m) (an idempotent localisation keeps the dévissage and the marked primes), and the étale map makes B→C_q faithfully flat. It does not duplicate lem-pc-flat-module-on-later-stage, which needs Noetherian stages. Neither new node restates the item.
